mechanism: Stop-loss orders and exchange liquidation prices are positive-feedback, price-contingent market orders that rest just BEYOND salient levels (Osler, NY Fed SR150: stop-loss buy orders cluster just above levels, stop-loss sells just below). The most salient level on a 1h chart is the prior 3-day (72 closed 1h bars) extreme: shorts who sold the range put their buy-stops, and their liquidation prices, just above it. When a 1h bar trades through that extreme, those orders fire as forced market buys (a stop/liquidation sweep). If the forced flow is the only thing driving the break, it is absorbed by resting limit sellers and the bar CLOSES back inside the prior range: the fuel is spent (the stops that were resting there no longer exist), and the traders who chased the new high are now long above a failed level with their own stops just below it, which become the next forced flow in the opposite direction. The signal fades the sweep: short after an upside sweep that closes back below the prior 72-bar high, long after a downside sweep that closes back above the prior 72-bar low, held up to 24 hours. It differs from a breakout (close beyond the extreme), which the probe shows continues for ~12h instead.
counterparty: (1) Stopped-out shorts and liquidated high-leverage shorts (longs on the downside) whose buy-stops / liquidation prices sat just beyond the prior 3-day extreme: they are forced to buy at market at the local worst price by their own contingent orders or by the exchange liquidation engine, and that liquidity is sold to them by resting limit sellers; (2) breakout-chasers who bought the new high and are trapped when the bar closes back inside the range, whose protective stops just below the old level become the next forced flow the fade position profits from.
prediction: On mr_edge TRAIN (2026-06-01 to ~2026-08-10, 1h bars, BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE), fading a closed 1h bar that pierces the prior 72-bar high (low) but closes back inside it, with tp=sl=150 bps and a 24-bar max hold, yields n >= 30 admitted trades whose mean net bps (after c=11.5) is > 0 with bootstrap CI95 excluding 0, and win rate >= fee_math.p_star(150) = 0.5383. Falsified if the CI includes 0, the mean is <= 0, or WR < 0.5383.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: S/R bounce fades price AT a 2-touch pivot zone before it breaks (zone as support, betting nobody pushes through). This thesis requires price to trade THROUGH the level (the stops beyond it are consumed) and then close back inside; the trade is on exhaustion of the triggered contingent-order flow, not on the level holding. A bar that touches but does not exceed the prior extreme is never a signal.

Liquidation-cascade reversion is triggered by an abnormal-volatility/volume bar anywhere and bets it reverts; it died because high-vol bars continue. This trigger has no volatility or volume condition; it is defined by WHERE the bar trades (beyond the 72-bar extreme, where stops sit) and by the close failing back inside. Bars that close beyond the extreme (the continuing cascade) are excluded by construction; the probe shows those continue for ~12h (probe_sweep_reclaim.out.txt breakout_hold).
Liq-cascade continuation bets that abnormal vol+volume bars continue; this bets on the opposite case, a failed sweep, selected by level geometry, not by bar size.
1h vol-expansion fade selects on range expansion; this selects on penetration of a prior extreme plus a close back inside, regardless of range; no volatility filter at all.
Multi-day mean reversion fades multi-day returns over multi-day holds; this is a single-bar event (failed sweep of stops) with a <=24h hold, and ordinary closes beyond the extreme are not faded.

Donchian trend follows closes beyond N-period extremes (a demoted book, not re-proposed). This trades only the complementary event: the extreme is pierced intrabar but the close fails back inside; a Donchian breakout bar can never be a signal here.

Prior-day value-area edge breakout was a breakout (continuation) off volume-profile edges with no backtest; this is a fade of a failed penetration of the 72-bar price extreme, pre-registered with a DOA line.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Stop-sweep exhaustion fade (closed 1h bars only).
    Upside sweep: this closed bar's high trades ABOVE the highest high of the prior 72 closed bars
    (where buy-stops / short-liquidation orders rest) but the bar CLOSES back below that prior high
    -> -1 (short). Downside sweep mirror -> +1 (long). A bar that sweeps both sides -> 0."""
    n = 72
    prior_high = df["high"].rolling(n, min_periods=n).max().shift(1)
    prior_low = df["low"].rolling(n, min_periods=n).min().shift(1)
    up = (df["high"] > prior_high) & (df["close"] < prior_high)
    dn = (df["low"] < prior_low) & (df["close"] > prior_low)
    out = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    out[up & ~dn] = -1
    out[dn & ~up] = 1
    return out
